Timestamp Notes

  1. Audio: a YouTube link or a file.
  2. Words and chords: paste them from Ultimate Guitar and Convert.
  3. Sections, bars, chords: S as each section starts, B on every downbeat, N on every chord change — or all three at once from a MIDI keyboard.
  4. Send on: to the Notation page for the melody, or the Backing Track for a style.

Every part folds; drag its ⠿ grip, or click ⇄, to move it to the other column.

New here? How to map a recording, step by step, including what to do when YouTube won't play a video.

Chord grid

    Chord timing and MIDI

    N as each chord starts (Shift+N takes the last one back): which chord it is comes from the words, so only the timing matters. Or all at once from a MIDI keyboard: the left hand plays one note on every barline and two notes together where a section starts; the right hand plays the chords. Only when notes start counts, and the left hand's pitches don't matter.

    The MIDI keyboard connects in the sidebar on the right.

    Words and chords

    Paste a song from Ultimate Guitar (chords on the line above the words, [Verse 1] headings) and Convert: the chords go into the words as ChordPro, and the headings become the sections to stamp.

    Sections from the words

    While it plays, press S as each section starts: it stamps the next one on this list.

      Send on

      With the bars tapped, each section's chords are spread over its bars, at the tapped tempo.

      Bar map

      While it plays, press B on the first beat of every bar. Backspace takes back the last tap; tapping a bar again replaces it. A missed tap shows as a long bar: Fill gaps puts it in. Tapped in 4 but it's really in 2 (or the other way)? Halve or Double the bars. A bar in another meter (a 2/4 bar, a 3/4 bridge): set its Beats in the Bars table.

      Sections

      Each section stamp (S) starts its section on the tapped bar nearest it. Open a section for its choruses (a head or a solo), and a chorus for its bars. ✎ beside any time corrects it: type the time and press Return, or press a letter (or a key on the MIDI keyboard) as the playhead reaches it; Space plays meanwhile, ↑ ↓ nudge. Shift+L loops the section under the playhead.

        No sections yet: stamp one with S.

        Phrases

        Transcribe a phrase at a time. Each section is cut into phrases; a phrase loops from its lead-in (the pickup: how many beats before its first downbeat the melody starts, up to two bars) to the next downbeat. P loops the phrase under the playhead, , . the one before or after, - = shorten or lengthen its lead-in, T (or Notate) goes to it on the Notation page, whose Back to the recording loops the next one here. With Phrases as chunks each phrase is a chunk there (V1a, V1b ...), and Shift+Space there plays this recording from the note being written. Slow it down with the player's speed.

          No phrases yet: tap the bars and stamp the sections.

          Bars

          The chords of each confirmed section, a cell a beat (. holds the chord on): the same as the grids written into the ChordPro at each pause, where they can be changed by hand.

          Timestamps

          S stamps a section: choose its label (Head, Verse, Sax solo, A, A′, B … or Other to type one); a label that comes again is numbered everywhere (Head 1, Head 2). C stamps a note. Click a time to jump to it, × to delete it. Shift+click to type a new one. Space or Return plays and pauses; ← → or h l go 5 seconds back or on. Leave a note with Esc or jk.
